userStories.title: Contract and server read model
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the strict transcript metadata schema widened and the transcript API to project a server-derived operator display name, so that operator rows are safely readable before any writer exists.
acceptanceCriteria: nodeTranscriptMetadataSchema (packages/workflows/src/schemas/node-execution.ts:29) accepts optional origin: z.literal('operator') and optional nullable operator_user_id alongside the existing message_id; tests prove a full operator triple parses, an explicit null sender parses, origin 'assistant' fails, and an unknown sibling key still fails (.strict() not weakened); keys are not made conditionally dependent

getUserDisplayNamesByIds exported from packages/core/src/db/users.ts deduplicates ids, returns [] without querying on empty input, selects only id and display_name from remote_agent_users with positional parameters, and chunks distinct ids into sequential queries of at most 500; tests assert exact SQL/params for one chunk, one placeholder for duplicate ids, and two bounded queries for 501 ids; no cache added

workflowNodeMessageTextResponseSchema (packages/server/src/routes/schemas/workflow.schemas.ts:194) gains operator_display_name: z.string().nullable().optional() on the text variant only; tool/status variants unchanged

api.ts list compatibility branch, cursor branch (applied to the page after removing the limit+1 overflow row), and detail route all enrich only operator text rows: trimmed non-blank display name, else senderId.slice(0, 8), else explicit null for null sender; the field is omitted entirely on non-operator rows; exactly one batch lookup per response (no N+1); the overflow row triggers no lookup

On batch-helper rejection the routes still return 200, build the map entirely from short ids, and log exactly one workflow_node_operator_names_lookup_failed warning containing runId, nodeId, distinct sender count, and errorType — never message text, display names, the error message, or the raw sender-id set

api.workflow-runs.test.ts gains mockGetUserDisplayNamesByIds and a named mockApiLogWarn (reset in the transcript-route beforeEach) covering: name trimming, blank/missing-user fallback, null identity, non-operator omission, two ids across three rows in one batch, cursor overflow exclusion, detail projection, and rejection with one safe warning; all pre-existing fixture and paging assertions still pass

packages/web/src/lib/api.generated.d.ts regenerated against this worktree's server; the diff contains only origin + operator_user_id in transcript metadata and nullable optional operator_display_name on the text row; the temporary server is stopped afterwards

AD-12 in ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md, steering-test-plan.md, and steering-api-contract.md amended to match Story 2.8 (server owns the short-id fallback; null reserved for identity-less rows; executor not route writes the row; stored triple vs response-only field distinguished)

Focused verification passes: bun test src/schemas/node-execution.test.ts (workflows), bun test src/db/users.test.ts (core), bun test src/routes/api.workflow-runs.test.ts (server), bun run type-check, bun run lint --max-warnings 0, and bun --filter @archon/server test
No executor code writes the new metadata yet; no SQL schema, migration, transcript-store, send-route, or new server helper module is added
userStories.technicalNotes: Phase 1 of the plan (phase-01-contract-and-server-read-model.md). Tests first for the schema keys, then schema edit, then the users helper, then wire projection in api.ts (helpers stay local to api.ts — no new module), then doc reconciliation, then OpenAPI regeneration. Story 2.8 beats stale AD-12 wording: server falls back to the 8-char short id, not null. Read the phase file for the full file table and per-test list.
userStories.notes: Implemented in iteration 1. Files: packages/workflows/src/schemas/node-execution.ts, node-execution.test.ts, packages/core/src/db/users.ts, users.test.ts, packages/server/src/routes/schemas/workflow.schemas.ts, api.ts, api.workflow-runs.test.ts, packages/web/src/lib/api.generated.d.ts, ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md AD-12, steering-test-plan.md, steering-api-contract.md.

userStories.title: Web read model and both shell renderers
userStories.description: As a transcript reader, I want the web history core to recognize operator rows and both node-room shells to render them with the final approved anatomy, so that human guidance is visibly distinct from agent prose without relying on color.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentHistoryItem (packages/web/src/lib/agent-history.ts:27) gains a member { kind: 'operator'; id; seq; role: 'operator'; text; operatorUserId: string | null; operatorDisplayName: string | null; messageId: string | null; delivery: 'sent'; execution: TranscriptExecution | null }

buildAgentHistory (:304) branches on message.kind === 'text' && message.metadata?.origin === 'operator' after tool-card handling and before the generic text branch; text is verbatim (no trim/transform, no presentedText, no Markdown, no todo folding, no tool pairing); display name = non-blank response field else first 8 chars of a non-null sender id else null (compat guard only — performs no request); messageId and execution scope carried; delivery is the literal 'sent'

agent-history.test.ts proves: verbatim whitespace/newlines/Markdown markers; a one-property output_format envelope stays serialized for the operator while an adjacent assistant row still presents normally; response name wins, blank/missing falls back to 8-char id, null identity stays null; message_id and execution survive; an operator row between assistant deltas stays a separate item in seq order; todo folding ignores operator prose; existing assistant/tool expectations unchanged

NodeRoom.tsx adds an OperatorHistory component beside AssistantHistory and an explicit item.kind === 'operator' branch before the final lifecycle branch, reusing the row wrapper, focus ring, data-last-row, and renderAfterItem; DOM contract: wrapper data-operator-row with overflow-wrap:anywhere; role line flex/full-width/10px/tracking 0.07em/uppercase CSS transform over lowercase DOM/text-secondary/margins 10px 2px 3px; data-operator-label renders 'operator' plus ' · <name>' only when non-null; data-operator-delivery margin-left:auto/flex-shrink:0/11px/normal case/tracking/text-secondary/literal 'sent'; data-operator-body font-sans/12.5px/line-height 1.55/normal weight/text-primary/whitespace-pre-wrap/margins 0 2px 6px rendering {item.text} directly (never ReactMarkdown)
AssistantHistory in the same file is corrected to lowercase DOM 'assistant', a 10px/0.07em text-secondary role line, and a 12.5px/1.55 text-secondary body while keeping Markdown rendering

LegacyNodeRoom.test.tsx proves: label, right-aligned lowercase sent, raw body text with no elements created from operator input; markup-like display names escaped as text; tool/interrupted -> operator -> assistant order via compareDocumentPosition; null identity renders exactly 'operator' with no separator; operator as final item keeps data-last-row and tabindex=-1; class/token assertions encode approved size, line height, weight, strengths, casing mechanism, and absence of border/pill; assistant label source lowercase and body text-secondary

ConsoleAgentHistoryList.tsx adds the same local OperatorHistory + explicit branch + identical assistant correction; historyItemRowVisible is NOT modified (already true for non-tool/lifecycle) — a component test asserts the operator row stays visible when showToolCalls and showSystem are false
ConsoleNodeRoom.test.tsx repeats the contract-bearing DOM/class assertions independently of Legacy coverage and proves an operator item last under hidden filters still receives focus-marker selection

A repo search for AgentHistoryItem/item.kind/kind switches finds no consumer needing a new branch where fallthrough is already correct; no changes to project-text-transcript.ts, pair-tool-transcript.ts, occurrence-groups.ts, steering dock state; no cross-shell component created

Rejected draft styling (9.5px tertiary label, text-sm body, medium weight, bordered uppercase status pill, bubble/avatar/role hue) appears nowhere; verification passes: bun test src/lib/agent-history.test.ts, NODE_ENV=development bun test for both room specs, packages/web bun run type-check, bun run lint --max-warnings 0, and bun --filter @archon/web test

userStories.title: Executor persistence and ordering
userStories.description: As an auditor, I want the direct and loop executors to append one verbatim operator row per drained message under the caused turn's attempt at the first provider-stream yield or normal empty completion, so that ordering, attribution, and prompt stability are provable.
acceptanceCriteria: appendOperatorTranscript added beside appendToolResultTranscript in packages/workflows/src/node-transcript.ts takes run id, node_id (executor stepName), the current transcript execution scope, and readonly QueuedOperatorMessage[]; for each message in array order it awaits appendNodeTranscript with kind 'text', payload { text: message.message } verbatim, and metadata transcriptMetadata(scope, { origin: 'operator', operator_user_id: message.operatorUserId, message_id: message.messageId }); QueuedOperatorMessage is a type-only import from steering-registry.ts; no trim/combine/retry/status/event/stream fields and no extra catch/log layer

node-transcript.test.ts proves the exact row shape for two differently attributed messages, explicit operator_user_id: null (not omission), no stream fields, preserved whitespace, and that a rejecting first append still allows the second to be attempted and the helper to resolve (fail-open continuation via appendNodeTranscript)

Direct path in dag-executor.ts carries turnGuidanceMessages: readonly QueuedOperatorMessage[] assigned at both delivery points (interrupt wake kind === 'send_now' and natural steeringHandle.drain()) instead of joining immediately; at the guidance head after executionScope = newTranscriptAttempt(executionScope) and before reaskPrompt = turnPrompt it derives turnPrompt via the unchanged messages.map(m => m.message).join('\n\n') and retains a pending receipt context {rotated scope, messages}; session id, turnIsGuidance, settlement, and continue turns behavior unchanged

The context is passed only to guidance turn pass zero of runStreamPass; inside the provider-stream try, appendOperatorTranscript is awaited immediately before processing the first yielded MessageChunk (context then marked recorded) or immediately after a normally-empty for-await completes; a stream startup throw before either seam writes no operator row; the context is never passed to a structured-output re-ask, so re-asks cannot duplicate rows; no second catch around the provider

Loop path mirrors this: message-array state next to turnGuidancePrompt, both loop drain-site joins replaced with array assignment, at the loop guidance head after iterationExecutionScope = newTranscriptAttempt(...) derive the unchanged double-newline prompt and retain the context with iterationExecutionScope and the executor's namespaced stepName; append at the same first-yield/normal-empty-completion seam on re-ask attempt zero; template substitution, loop variables, iteration accounting, completion re-evaluation, re-asks, and session threading untouched; a guidance turn never consumes an iteration

dag-executor.test.ts extends the existing #181/#183 harnesses (no nine duplicate workflows) using a typed kind === 'text' && metadata?.origin === 'operator' predicate and proves the full matrix: direct natural drain two-sender FIFO order and seq placement (last prior-turn seq < operator seqs < caused assistant seq, shared caused attempt, identical double-newline prompt); direct interrupt -> idle -> Send now (interrupted seq < operator rows < resumed echo, caller ids preserved, resumed not interrupted attempt); loop natural drain (inside current iteration ancestry, precede caused output, no iteration consumed); loop interrupt redirect; loop-group body uses namespaced node_id proving stepName plumbing; null identity writes explicit null; structured-output re-ask yields exactly one operator row; cancel/discard, resumability failure before drain, and provider startup throw each write no row; one-of-three append rejection still completes the node with the other two audit rows and the provider receiving all three messages in order

Two direct-path seam tests prove: a provider throwing before its first yield writes no operator row and follows the existing node-failure path; a provider whose first yield is held shows beginTurn already registered, then on release the operator append completes before that first chunk enters the transcript

All pre-existing #181/#183 assertions preserved (session continuity, node lifecycle, interrupt classification, no extra turn-start event); no changes to registry, send/interrupt routes, store/database, migrations, providers, or the workflow event model

Verification passes: bun test src/node-transcript.test.ts, bun test src/dag-executor.test.ts -t 'operator', full bun test src/dag-executor.test.ts, bun test src/steering-registry.test.ts, packages/workflows bun run type-check, bun run lint --max-warnings 0; package test script used for broader coverage; diagnostic runs use an empty temporary ARCHON_HOME
Rows written here are readable/renderable by the US-001/US-002 code already landed
userStories.technicalNotes: Phase 3 (phase-03-executor-persistence.md). The writer turns on only after the read side is safe. userStories.title: Integration, rollout, and closeout
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the existing steering Playwright journeys converted to positive outside-in proof with visual acceptance on both shells, repository gates run, and Story 2.8 closed with an accurate evidence record.
acceptanceCriteria: e2e/lib/playwright/run-detail.ts widens the listNodeMessages return type (id, seq, kind, payload, optional created_at, optional top-level operator_display_name: string | null, metadata origin/operator_user_id/message_id/execution occurrence+attempt) matching the generated response contract; type-only change, no any

Each [V:steer.direct-{surface}] test in e2e/ui/agent-queue-guidance.spec.ts: sets X-Archon-User: E2E_STARTER_WEB_USER before navigation; retains the two caller message_ids; deletes the obsolete operator-rows-absent assertions/comments; asserts exactly two operator rows in seq order with verbatim bodies (including the embedded fake-provider directive), captured ids, identical non-empty sender ids, operator_display_name === 'e2e-starter', preceding the caused echo and sharing its attempt_id (different from the settled prior attempt); on room reopen asserts two [data-operator-row] with label source 'operator · e2e-starter', status 'sent', plain body before the echo in DOM order; all existing session/queue/focus/a11y assertions kept

Each [V:steer.interrupt-{surface}] test in e2e/ui/agent-interrupt-redirect.spec.ts: applies the starter header before any send; captures all three message_ids via trackPosts(...).bodies(); asserts three operator API rows in order with the full metadata triple and e2e-starter projection; interrupted status seq < first operator row seq, resumed echo seq > last; all operator rows use the resumed echo attempt, not the interrupted attempt; fresh-room DOM order interrupted tool -> three operator rows -> resumed echo proven via Node.compareDocumentPosition (not boundingBox().y); every status exactly 'sent' and no 'delivered' string anywhere

[V:steer.interrupt-visual-{surface}] extended (no new spec): a long multiline first queued message; at 460x900 asserts/captures no room overflow, role-line source + uppercase computed transform + secondary color + 10px + ~0.07em tracking, sent computed normal case/11px/secondary/right-aligned/visible, body preserved text/sans/12.5px/line-height 1.55/normal weight/primary/no Markdown child, adjacent assistant body 12.5px/1.55 secondary, interrupted->operator->assistant DOM order and last-row reachability; the same operator-row capture repeats after the existing 1440x900 Send now flow on both Legacy and Console; new captures land in this plan's evidence dir via a second constant or dir parameter without moving #181/#183 evidence
No third spec, no copied steering helpers, no additional full workflow run added

Gates run cheapest-first then full: bun --filter @archon/core test, @archon/workflows test, @archon/server test, @archon/web test, bun run type-check, bun run lint --max-warnings 0, bun run build:web, cd e2e && npm run typecheck, ARCHON_E2E_REPO_ROOT=<abs root> npx playwright test -c playwright.config.ts --grep '\[V:steer\.(direct|interrupt|interrupt-visual)-', then both spec files, then bun run validate; root bun test never substitutes for bun run validate; no check:schema-upgrades (no SQL change); every spawned server/test process tracked and stopped

reports/acceptance-evidence.md written inside the plan directory from completed runs only: each parent-plan acceptance criterion mapped to its proving test(s), focused test + bun run validate summaries, Playwright command/result with links to 460/1440 captures for both surfaces, generated-type diff review, explicit no-migration/no-backfill statement, and rollout (drain active steering turns, deploy complete reader+writer build, reload open node-room tabs) plus downgrade-safe rollback instructions (disable writer, keep widened parser, or forward-fix; never delete audit rows)
_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/agent-node-room/sprint-status.yaml:75 set to 2-8-see-operator-messages-in-the-transcript: done only after all gates pass; no other story status touched

If publication is requested, PR opened against develop with the repository template copied into the body (Problem and outcome, Review guidance, Solution, Behavior change, Validation, rollout/rollback implications, Closes #188; unused sections/comments deleted) and bun run validate green beforehand
userStories.technicalNotes: Phase 4 (phase-04-integration-rollout-and-closeout.md). Reuse e2e/ui/agent-queue-guidance.spec.ts and agent-interrupt-redirect.spec.ts — they already cover natural drain, FIFO queueing, Stop, Send now, interrupted tool state, resumed echo, and 460/1440 captures on both surfaces. E2E_STARTER_WEB_USER is the seeded user whose display name is 'e2e-starter'; archon.startWorkflowViaWeb already uses that identity but the default Playwright page needs the X-Archon-User header before navigation for browser-originated sends. Playwright's worker fixture owns its server; reconcile only this worktree's PIDs/ports on cleanup bypass.
